body:
`.claude/skills/issue-lanes/SKILL.md:325-333` documents the MECHANISM of `adlc ticket complete` correctly and completely: it is a base-branch admin act, rails-guard refuses `completed: true` inside any PR so it can only land as a direct push to main, it writes a new `.adlc/manifest.d/` segment, other open PRs branched from an older main then red with `… exists at base but is absent at HEAD — committed segments cannot be removed or renamed in a PR`, that is a false positive from staleness, and a rebase clears it.

WHAT IS MISSING is WHEN to complete relative to an open PR queue. The bullet says "ask before doing this" and stops. Nothing tells the operator whether to complete immediately after a merge or hold until the queue drains.

WHY THIS MATTERS — two sessions derived OPPOSITE rules from the same docs on 2026-09-19, each from having seen only one failure:
- From watching rails freeze: "complete immediately, it is not optional housekeeping." Wrong alone — it pushes a segment into an open queue with no warning.
- From watching a PR queue: "batch the completes until the queue drains." Wrong alone, and worse — it invites the frozen-rails failure.

MEASURED EVIDENCE FOR BOTH HALVES, use these numbers, they are verified:
- Frozen rails: ticket T-01M1KT58RQE7SEVJMG00YK235J shipped in PR #973 (merged 2026-09-04T01:20:46Z, commit 6bf8841c) and was never completed. Rails are unioned across every NON-COMPLETED ticket, so its six frozen paths (context-handoff adapter/bypass-grant/deny-lifecycle/handoff bin, cli registry/help) blocked an UNRELATED lane from editing a single comment. Completed 2026-09-16 as 639f3e53. Verified elapsed: TWELVE DAYS.
- No net rebase burden: the `main protection` ruleset (id 17662766) sets `strict_required_status_checks_policy: true` with required checks `test (18|20|22)`. Read live from `gh api repos/voodootikigod/adlc/rulesets/17662766`. BEHIND therefore already blocks every merge, so the rebase was owed regardless of anyone's completion. The completion changes only WHEN staleness surfaces and HOW IT READS — the message looks like an integrity violation, so an unfamiliar reader burns time proving they deleted nothing. The cost is diagnostic noise, not work.

WHAT TO BUILD — extend the existing bullet at SKILL.md:325-333 with the four-point timing rule. Do NOT rewrite the mechanism text above it; it is correct and hard-won.
1. Complete promptly. Frozen rails blocking unrelated lanes is the worse failure; cite the twelve-day incident.
2. Enumerate who it lands on BEFORE pushing: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <segment-commit> <pr-head>` per open PR; true means that PR already contains the segment and is unaffected.
3. Announce rather than defer, because the strict policy means the rebase is owed anyway — you are saving them a false-alarm diagnosis, not saving them work.
4. Wait ONLY for something time-critical in flight (a queue-unblocking hotfix), never as a general batching policy.

Match the file's existing voice: dense, imperative, evidence-carrying, second person. It is an operator runbook, not prose.

RAILS: `plugins/adlc-claude-code/skills/adlc/SKILL.md`. That is the generated phase-router skill, frozen by the routing/consolidation guard (`scripts/router/check-consolidation.mjs`) — adding a routing token there fails that guard. This ticket touches the issue-lanes OPERATOR skill only. If the router seems to need editing, stop and say so.

ALSO IN SCOPE (widened after the owner of #1051 asked for it): a SECOND note, in the "Gotchas that are not in the ticket bodies" section, carrying the #1051 diagnostic heuristic. It is deliberately separate from the timing rule above because it teaches a different thing and is useful whether or not a merge queue is ever enabled:

  A GREEN PR IS NOT EVIDENCE main WILL BE GREEN AFTER IT MERGES. `strict_required_status_checks_policy` evaluates up-to-dateness at MERGE TIME against the base tip, not against the prospective merged state, so two individually-green PRs can merge minutes apart and leave main red. Measured: PR #1046 merged 2026-09-19T16:35:58Z adding `scripts/test/tmp-fixture-boundary.test.mjs`; PR #1034 merged 16:36:10Z, TWELVE SECONDS later. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 051c1812 dad19f26` is false and `git ls-tree -r dad19f26 -- scripts/test/tmp-fixture-boundary.test.mjs` is empty — the guard did not exist on the head that PR's CI ran, so it could not have flagged the file it later flagged on main. WHEN main REDS RIGHT AFTER A MERGE, CHECK FOR A SAME-MINUTE NEIGHBOUR BEFORE HUNTING A BUG IN YOUR OWN DIFF. Two sessions each burned a round on this, hours apart. A merge queue is the structural fix (it re-runs required checks against the prospective merged state) and is tracked in #1051; do NOT propose the config change here, only the heuristic.

ACCEPTANCE
1. SKILL.md:325-333's mechanism text is unchanged; verify with `git diff` showing only an addition.
2. All four points present, each with its reason, not bare imperatives.
3. The twelve-day figure and the ruleset field name appear, so the rule carries its evidence.
4. `node --test scripts/test/*.test.mjs` green — in particular the consolidation/router guards, proving the router skill was not disturbed.
5. `npm test` green from the repo root, output shown.
6. `adlc rails-guard --base origin/main --ticket <this ticket id>` exits 0.
7. The mutation gate is VACUOUS on a docs-only diff ("no source files changed" / comment-only) and must be reported as such, never cited as evidence of correctness.
title: issue-lanes: document WHEN to run ticket complete relative to an open PR queue
